title: Partner onboarding — PDB through Pathfinder
subtitle: End-to-end architecture walkthrough: Kubernetes PodDisruptionBudget YAML → ADR obligation → binding → normalized evidence → assess → publish. Dense on purpose; skim the rail, deepen per step.

glossary.binding: Approved mapping from a reviewed obligation to a catalog requirement + pattern_id + verifier. Stored in the obligation review registry; stale digests force re-review.
glossary.IssueSurface: assess-repo --issue-surface (GitHub issue / sandbox). Manual-review and missing analyzer evidence become NOT_APPLICABLE so unresolved judgment does not pollute the automated verdict. Repo CI keeps IssueSurface=false.
glossary.NOT_APPLICABLE: Requirement status meaning the check does not apply in this context (empty scope, issue-surface N/A, or analyzer not collected for the issue). All-NOT_APPLICABLE still rolls up to INDETERMINATE — nothing was proved.
glossary.REVIEW_REQUIRED: Repo-CI status for manual-review verifiers: a human must decide. On IssueSurface this becomes NOT_APPLICABLE instead.
glossary.EVIDENCE_MISSING: Fail-closed status when a required analyzer scan is incomplete or digests are missing (repo CI). On IssueSurface, missing analyzer evidence for that analyzer is NOT_APPLICABLE.
glossary.pattern_id: Reusable verification pattern from adr/patterns.json (e.g. security.source_pattern, configuration.authentication, manual_review). Gates which verifier_types may bind.
glossary.pattern_hint: Deterministic extract suggestion on a Candidate before human review. Heuristic only — never executable approval.
glossary.analyzer-rule: Verifier type that matches pinned OpenGrep or Checkov ScanResult findings by exact rule_ids, path/extension scope, and complete digests.
glossary.CKV_*: Bare Checkov rule IDs after normalization (CKV_AWS_*, CKV_K8S_*, CKV2_*). Catalog bindings today pin CKV_AWS_*; kubernetes framework is enabled in rules/checkov.yml.
glossary.ScanResult: Normalized analyzer output in internal/analyzer: status, analyzers[], findings[], scanned_paths, binary/config/input/raw_output SHA-256 digests.
glossary.Candidate: Unapproved obligation extracted from ADR Decision prose — citation, modality, confidence, pattern_hint. executable stays false until human bind.
glossary.enforcement_mode: blocking | advisory | review_required on an approved binding. Only blocking feeds the --enforce-blocking CI gate.
glossary.runtime_llm_calls: Must stay 0 on assess workflows. workshop-emit --enforce-assess-llm fails the snapshot otherwise. Assist is batch-time only.
glossary.manual_review: Pattern id and verifier path for subjective obligations with no reliable analyzer proxy. Repo CI → REVIEW_REQUIRED; IssueSurface → NOT_APPLICABLE.
glossary.submission_kind: First-class input shape on assessment results and candidates: tech_spec (ADR / English prose) vs code_snippet (source or IaC). Orthogonal to EvidenceMode and IssueSurface. Empty = unspecified (older data). KPI splits: kpi.assess.submission_kind, kpi.submission.*_count, kpi.escalation.rate.{tech_spec,code_snippet}.

steps.title: Start from a code_snippet submission (PDB YAML)
steps.why: Partners need a concrete artifact before abstractions. Here is a critical Deployment’s PodDisruptionBudget — a [[submission_kind]]=code_snippet entering Pathfinder’s Checkov path (not English tech-spec prose).
steps.technical:
submission_kind=code_snippet marks source/IaC evidence. Pathfinder never executes submitted YAML. On the GitHub [[IssueSurface]], fences are materialized into a sandbox tree and auto-classify as code_snippet when the body is fence-only; on repo CI, assess-repo defaults to code_snippet while Checkov scans the live tree under pinned binary/ruleset digests. Kubernetes is an enabled Checkov framework in rules/checkov.yml alongside terraform, cloudformation, and dockerfile.

Notice minAvailable: 2 against a 3-replica Deployment — majority availability during voluntary eviction. maxUnavailable would be the alternate control when replica count is small.
notice: submission_kind=code_snippet (YAML/TF/source) — distinct from tech_spec prose parsers
apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec are what Checkov’s kubernetes parser sees
selector must match the Deployment’s pod labels or the PDB is a no-op
This file is the later ScanResult.findings[].path target
callouts: Workshop fixture — illustrative payments-api PDB, not a live corpus ADR yet.

panels.title: deploy/payments-api-pdb.yaml
panels.caption: Voluntary disruption budget for a labeled critical Deployment.
panels.code:
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: payments-api-pdb
  namespace: payments
  labels:
    app: payments-api
    pathfinder.critical: "true"
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments-api
  namespace: payments
  labels:
    app: payments-api
    pathfinder.critical: "true"
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payments-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: ghcr.io/example/payments-api:1.4.2

deeper.title: Deeper dive — why Checkov, not OpenGrep?
deeper.body: OpenGrep (rules/pathfinder-security.yml) targets source AST / structural code patterns — SQL format strings, AWS SDK misuse, secrets. A PodDisruptionBudget is declarative IaC. Checkov’s kubernetes framework evaluates resource shape; OpenGrep would be the wrong parser family here. Subjective product policy with no observable proxy stays [[manual_review]] / verifier type manual-review.

panels.title: Analyzer selection cheat-sheet
panels.code:
Source / security AST  →  OpenGrep  + analyzer-rule (rules.pathfinder.*)
Terraform / CFN / K8s / Dockerfile  →  Checkov  + analyzer-rule (CKV_*)
JSON keys / numeric bounds  →  json-required-keys | json-number-range
Subjective / no proxy  →  manual-review  (repo: REVIEW_REQUIRED; issue: NOT_APPLICABLE)

steps.title: Write the tech_spec submission (ADR obligation)
steps.why: YAML alone is not policy. An accepted ADR Decision is a [[submission_kind]]=tech_spec — English prose that extract/ingest parsers handle differently from code fences.
steps.technical:
submission_kind=tech_spec marks ADR / tech-spec English. ingest-adrs indexes Markdown with an H1 title, Status, and Decision section; extract-obligations tags each Candidate with submission_kind=tech_spec. Later stages bind citations via source_path, source_line_start/end, and source_sha256 of file bytes. RFC 2119 modality (MUST / SHALL) drives extract confidence; SHOULD softens the band.

The three-layer model: (1) Source ADR — immutable Markdown + digest; (2) Obligation — cited Candidate or approved interpretation; (3) Verification pattern — reusable analyzer/policy contract shared across many ADRs.

Contrast with the previous step: PDB YAML entered as code_snippet; this Decision prose enters as tech_spec so workshop KPIs can trend parsers separately.
notice: submission_kind=tech_spec (ADR/prose) — Goldmark ingest + English extract, not fence sandbox
Normative language lives in Decision — Context/Consequences are not extracted as obligations
Accepted status is required before a binding can block CI
Filename supplies stable document ID when the H1 lacks ADR-####

panels.title: ADR-2100.md (Decision excerpt)
panels.caption: Fixture-local ADR — corpus does not yet ship a PDB ADR; shape matches MADR + RFC 2119.
panels.code:
# ADR-2100: Pod Disruption Budgets for critical Deployments

## Status
Accepted

## Context
Node drains and cluster upgrades evict pods. Critical payment APIs
must keep a majority of desired replicas available during voluntary
disruptions.

## Decision
Critical Deployments MUST declare a PodDisruptionBudget that keeps
minAvailable at or above a majority of desired replicas, or sets
maxUnavailable to at most one when replica count is three or fewer.

## Consequences
- Platform Checkov/Kubernetes policy can verify PDB presence and bounds.
- Teams without a matching selector fail closed under blocking bindings.

deeper.title: Deeper dive — ingestion contract
deeper.body: Reprocessing the same content hash must not create duplicate documents. Assessment reports state which ADR and obligation versions were used. See docs/specification-to-enforcement.md and docs/scaling-adr-design.md.

steps.title: Extract a Candidate (not an approval)
steps.why: Deterministic extractors turn Decision prose into reviewable [[Candidate]] objects. Nothing here is executable; approval_status stays pending_review.
steps.technical:
extract-obligations emits an Index of Candidates. Confidence bands (high | medium | low) combine modality strength, [[pattern_hint]] match quality, and citation quality. Only the low band is eligible for batch LLM assist.

For this PDB wording, modality is must (strong) but Kubernetes policy matching is weak in today’s heuristic map — so confidence=low with escalation_reasons like weak_pattern_match and broad_scope. That is intentional: humans (or assist) decide the [[pattern_id]], extract never auto-binds.
notice: executable is always false until human bind
pattern_hint is a suggestion, not a binding
kpi.escalation.rate = confidence_low / candidate_total

steps.title: Choose the parser / analyzer binding
steps.why: This is the architectural fork partners must internalize: OpenGrep vs Checkov vs manual-review vs JSON verifiers. Humans record the [[binding]]; extract never invents one.
steps.technical:
record-obligation-review / accept-assist-proposal writes a ReviewRecord into the append-only registry: decision, pattern_id, requirement_id, requirement_sha256, [[enforcement_mode]].

Catalog Verifier.type decides runtime behavior:
• analyzer-rule + analyzer=checkov + rule_ids → require a complete Checkov [[ScanResult]]
• analyzer-rule + analyzer=opengrep → OpenGrep findings
• manual-review → [[REVIEW_REQUIRED]] in repo CI, [[NOT_APPLICABLE]] on [[IssueSurface]]
• json-required-keys / json-number-range → native Go JSON verifiers (pattern configuration.bounds_or_required_values)

Accuracy note: today’s corpus pins CKV_AWS_* against Terraform fixtures. Kubernetes is enabled in Checkov config, but there is no catalogued PDB [[CKV_*]] yet — so a honest partner binding is either manual-review now, or a proposed analyzer-rule awaiting a real rule_id + fixtures.
commands: adrctl accept-assist-proposal --proposal-id PROP-PDB-1 --decision approved --pattern-id manual_review --enforcement-mode review_required --requirement-id REQ-PDB-1
notice: pattern_id must allow the verifier_types you intend (adr/patterns.json)
Stale requirement_sha256 or source digest → binding becomes stale → re-review
blocking enforcement_mode is what --enforce-blocking gates on

deeper.title: Deeper dive — BindingCoverage KPIs
deeper.body: validate-obligation-reviews / assess-obligations emit BindingCoverage: pending_review_count, approved_count, stale_count, orphaned_count, blocking_binding_count, unbound_count. Pending or stale blocking items fail --enforce-blocking.

steps.title: Normalize analyzer output to ScanResult
steps.why: Raw Checkov/OpenGrep SARIF is vendor-shaped. Pathfinder adapts it into [[ScanResult]] / evidence.Bundle with digests so assessment can fail closed on incomplete scans.
steps.technical:
scan-checkov / execute-plan produce JSON + raw SARIF. ParseSARIF fills findings with analyzer, rule_id, path, start_line, message, fingerprint. Digests required for analyzer-rule: binary_sha256, rule_set_sha256, configuration_sha256, input_sha256, raw_output_sha256, non-empty scanned_paths, status=COMPLETE.

Below: illustrative ScanResult as if a future PDB rule reported a finding on the YAML from step 1. Today’s CI proves Checkov with CKV_AWS_* on Terraform under testdata/analyzer-fixtures — same envelope, different rule_id.
notice: Incomplete digests → EVIDENCE_MISSING (repo) or NOT_APPLICABLE (IssueSurface missing analyzer)
rule_id matching is exact after Checkov ID normalization
evidence.Bundle.Record wraps findings with producer + provenance

panels.title: checkov-evidence.json — ScanResult (envelope)
panels.caption: internal/analyzer.ScanResult — digests make the scan replayable.

panels.title: Finding (PASS path — PDB present)
panels.caption: Empty findings for a matching rule_id means PASS once bound to analyzer-rule. A violation would appear as a Finding.

deeper.title: Deeper dive — OpenGrep contrast
deeper.body: If this obligation were a Go SQL string format rule, the plan runner would dispatch opengrep with rules.pathfinder.* IDs. Same ScanResult envelope; different analyzers[].name and rule_id namespace.

steps.title: Assess statuses & IssueSurface semantics
steps.why: Assessment joins catalog requirements with evidence and emits per-requirement statuses — still zero [[runtime_llm_calls]].
steps.technical:
assess-repo evaluates each RequirementResult: status ∈ PASS | FAIL | INDETERMINATE | [[NOT_APPLICABLE]] | [[REVIEW_REQUIRED]] | [[EVIDENCE_MISSING]] | UNSUPPORTED | ERROR, plus evidence[] and findings[].

[[IssueSurface]] flips semantics for partners building issue vs repo flows:
• manual-review → REVIEW_REQUIRED (repo) vs NOT_APPLICABLE (issue)
• analyzer-rule with no scan for that analyzer → EVIDENCE_MISSING (repo) vs NOT_APPLICABLE (issue)

Overall verdict: any FAIL wins; REVIEW_REQUIRED / EVIDENCE_MISSING / UNSUPPORTED force INDETERMINATE; all-NOT_APPLICABLE is still INDETERMINATE (nothing proved). assess-obligations then joins Candidates to produce obligation_verdict + CandidateAssessment rows.
notice: runtime_llm_calls must be 0 on assess
coverage_status COMPLETE|PARTIAL|NONE is independent of verdict
Rejected candidates become NOT_APPLICABLE on the obligation join

deeper.title: Deeper dive — obligation join
deeper.body: CandidateAssessment carries candidate_id, decision, pattern_id, enforcement_mode, status, evidence_status, reason, evidence[]. RepositoryVerdict stays distinct from ObligationVerdict when bindings are stale or pending.

steps.title: Emit workshop snapshot & command center
steps.why: Partners ship architecture by making runs inspectable: metrics, digdowns, this journey, and fail-closed LLM gates.
steps.technical:
workshop-emit writes latest.json, metrics.json, and linked artifacts. Workshop Publish appends metrics/runs.jsonl, stores snapshots/<run_id>/, updates manifest.json on the workshop-data branch. Pages serves the SPA; humans write back via Issues, PR templates, and workflow_dispatch — never via the static site holding secrets.

--enforce-assess-llm fails the snapshot if [[runtime_llm_calls]] ≠ 0. Sample journey JSON is promoted to data root when present beside the snapshot (scripts/workshop_publish_data.py).
notice: latest.json + metrics.json + runs.jsonl are the command-center spine
loadSampleJourney prefers the selected run’s sample-journey, then any snapshot, then root
Internal visibility by design
